---
title: "Fixed exogenous variables"
---

In a mediation model the treatment and the covariates are **exogenous**: nothing in the model
explains them. Their means, variances and covariances are parameters of the joint model, and
they carry no information about the paths. The `fixed_x` argument of `fit_sem()` stops
estimating them and holds them at their sample values, as lavaan's `fixed.x = TRUE` does. This
chapter shows exactly what that changes (the parameter count and the likelihood) and what it
does not (the estimates and standard errors of the structural parameters, that is the paths, the
residual variances and the intercepts of the other variables; the degrees of freedom; and the
chi-square), proves why, and shows which comparisons the engine then refuses.

| | |
|---|---|
| **You need** | Chapters 1 to 3 (the RAM matrices, the discrepancy, the moment count) and the multivariate normal density |
| **You get** | the moments `fixed_x` fixes and where they go in the RAM matrices, the factorization argument for equal structural estimates and standard errors (and what changes when only some exogenous variables are fixed), the conditional log likelihood derived and computed by hand, its parameter count, and the refusals with their messages |
| **Time** | about 45 minutes |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
# These chapters teach the joint likelihood and the covariance-first form of the engine, so every fit pins the
# 0.14.x settings. medfit 0.15.0 itself defaults to fixed_x = the exogenous variables and meanstructure = TRUE; the
# note at the end of chapter 1 and Section 6 of chapter 4 show what that changes. Pass an explicit value to a call to override the pin.
fit_sem <- function(model, data, ..., fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL) {
  medfit::fit_sem(model, data, ..., fixed_x = fixed_x, meanstructure = meanstructure)
}
rd <- function(x, d = 4) round(x, d)
d <- mediation_demo
n <- nrow(d)

# Two exogenous variables (treatment and covariate1) and two outcomes (mediator1 and outcome)
full <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
"
restricted <- paste0(full, "cp == 0\n")   # one restriction, so that df = 1 and the chi-square is not zero
```

## 1. Which moments are fixed

A variable is **exogenous** here if it appears only as a predictor, never as the target of a path
(`treatment` and `covariate1`). With `fixed_x = TRUE` every such variable is selected; a character
vector selects a subset. The selected variables' means, variances and the covariances among the
exogenous variables that involve a selected one become **fixed moments**: the engine gives them the
sample values (divisor $n$, so $S_{ff} = \frac1n\sum_i (x_i - \bar x)(x_i - \bar x)^\top$, the matrix
of Chapter 1) and no longer treats them as parameters.

```{r}
#| label: fixed-rows
fx <- fit_sem(full, d, meanstructure = TRUE, fixed_x = TRUE, information = "expected")
fx@internals$fixed_x
tidy(fx)[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error", "fixed_x")]
```

The last five rows are the fixed moments (the variances and covariance of the two exogenous variables, and,
because this fit has a mean structure, their two means). They are flagged `fixed_x = TRUE` and have no standard
error, because they are no longer estimates; the engine keeps them in its parameter table (`fx@table`). Check that they are the sample moments:

```{r}
#| label: fixed-values
exo <- c("treatment", "covariate1")
xm <- as.matrix(d[, exo])
s_ff <- cov(xm) * (n - 1) / n
tab <- fx@table
fixed_tab <- tab[tab$fixed_x, c("lhs", "op", "rhs", "est")]
fixed_tab$sample_value <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fixed_tab)), function(i) {
  row <- fixed_tab[i, ]
  if (row$op == "~1") colMeans(xm)[[row$lhs]] else s_ff[row$lhs, row$rhs]
}, numeric(1))
c(largest_difference = max(abs(fixed_tab$est - fixed_tab$sample_value)))
fixed_tab[, c("est", "sample_value")] <- rd(fixed_tab[, c("est", "sample_value")], 6)
fixed_tab
```

```{r}
#| label: fixed-values-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(nrow(fixed_tab) == 5L, max(abs(fixed_tab$est - fixed_tab$sample_value)) < 1e-6)
```

In the RAM matrices of Chapter 1 these entries of $S_{\text{ram}}$ and $m$ become constants, in the
same place a fixed value such as `y ~ 0.5*x` would sit; the parameter vector no longer has a slot for them.

## 2. Parameters, moments and degrees of freedom

Counting moments (Chapter 1): $p(p+1)/2$ distinct variances and covariances, plus $p$ means with a mean
structure. With $k$ fixed variables, the fixed moments are removed from the *count of moments* (the engine
does not ask the model to explain them) as well as from the *count of parameters*. Each removal is the
same size, so the difference, the degrees of freedom, does not change. Four fits to the restricted model:

```{r}
#| label: counts
fits <- list(
  free_cov = fit_sem(restricted, d),
  fixed_cov = fit_sem(restricted, d, fixed_x = TRUE),
  free_mean = fit_sem(restricted, d, meanstructure = TRUE),
  fixed_mean = fit_sem(restricted, d, meanstructure = TRUE, fixed_x = TRUE)
)
data.frame(
  fit = names(fits),
  parameters = vapply(fits, function(f) length(f@theta), numeric(1)),
  equality_rank = vapply(fits, function(f) f@internals$eq_rank, numeric(1)),
  fixed_moments = vapply(fits, function(f) f@internals$ram$n_fixed_x, numeric(1)),
  moments = vapply(fits, function(f) medfit:::.sem_moments(f@internals$ram), numeric(1)),
  df = vapply(fits, function(f) f@df, numeric(1)),
  chisq = vapply(fits, function(f) round(f@n_obs * f@f, 6), numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

```{r}
#| label: counts-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(all(vapply(fits, function(f) f@df, numeric(1)) == 1),
          diff(range(vapply(fits, function(f) f@n_obs * f@f, numeric(1)))) < 1e-6,
          all(vapply(fits, function(f) {
            medfit:::.sem_moments(f@internals$ram) - (length(f@theta) - f@internals$eq_rank) == f@df
          }, NA)))
```

With three variances and covariances fixed (covariance structure) the parameter count falls by 3 and the
moment count by 3; with the two means added it falls by 5 and 5. The degrees of freedom (1, from the one
restriction `cp == 0`) and the chi-square are identical in all four.

## 3. Why the estimates and standard errors do not change

This section proves the claim in the title for `fixed_x = TRUE`, checks it, and then shows what
changes when only some exogenous variables are fixed.

**Setup.** Take `fixed_x = TRUE`, so that $x$, the vector of the $k$ fixed variables, holds every
exogenous variable, and let $y$ be the vector of all other observed variables. No error of $y$
is correlated with $x$: such a covariance would be a statement about a fixed variable, which the engine
refuses (Section 5). In the RAM form, a variable with no incoming path is its own error plus its intercept:
$x = m_x + e_x$. So $x \sim N(\mu_x, \Sigma_{xx})$ with $\mu_x = m_x$ and $\Sigma_{xx} = S_{\text{ram},xx}$, and
nothing in the model touches these. Given $x$, the rest of the model is linear: $y = (I - A_{y y})^{-1}(m_y + A_{y x}\,x + e_y)$,
so

$$
y \mid x \;\sim\; N\bigl(c + \Gamma x,\; \Psi\bigr), \qquad
\Gamma = (I - A_{y y})^{-1} A_{y x}, \quad c = (I - A_{y y})^{-1} m_y, \quad
\Psi = (I - A_{y y})^{-1} S_{y y} (I - A_{y y})^{-\top}.
$$

Here $A_{y y}$ and $A_{y x}$ are the blocks of $A$, $S_{y y}$ is the error covariance of $y$, and $c$, $\Gamma$ and $\Psi$
depend only on the **structural parameters** $\psi$ (the paths, the residual variances, the intercepts of $y$) and not
on $\eta = (\mu_x, \Sigma_{xx})$.

**Step 1: factor the density.** For each row, $f(x_i, y_i) = f(y_i \mid x_i;\, \psi)\; f(x_i;\, \eta)$, the definition of a
conditional density. Taking logs and summing over rows,

$$
\ell(\psi, \eta) = \ell_c(\psi) + \ell_m(\eta),
$$

where $\ell_c$ is the conditional log likelihood of $y$ given $x$ and $\ell_m$ the marginal one of $x$. The two parts
have no parameter in common: this identity holds for every value of $(\psi, \eta)$.

**Step 2: maximize.** Because $\ell$ is a sum of a function of $\psi$ and a function of $\eta$, it is maximized by
maximizing each separately. The maximizer of $\ell_m$ is the sample mean and the divisor-$n$ covariance matrix of $x$ (the
standard result for the normal distribution). The maximizer $\hat\psi$ of $\ell_c$ does not involve $\eta$ at all. So the free
fit's structural estimates are $\hat\psi$. The fixed fit holds $\eta$ at $\hat\eta$ and maximizes the same $\ell$ over
$\psi$, which is $\ell_c(\psi)$ plus a constant: the same $\hat\psi$.

**Step 3: the information.** The cross second derivatives $\partial^2\ell/\partial\psi\,\partial\eta^\top$ are zero, because
$\partial\ell/\partial\psi = \partial\ell_c/\partial\psi$ does not depend on $\eta$. The information matrix is therefore
block diagonal, and its $\psi$ block is the information of $\ell_c$ alone. The covariance of $\hat\psi$ is the inverse of
that block, the same whether or not the $\eta$ block is present. So the standard errors of the structural estimates
agree between the two fits. The minimized discrepancy is the same too: the fixed fit's discrepancy is the free discrepancy of
Chapter 1 with $\eta$ set to $\hat\eta$, and the free optimum has $\eta = \hat\eta$ by Step 2, so the two minima are the
value of one function at one point. Hence the chi-square agrees.

Now check each step on our data. The estimates and standard errors of the structural parameters:

```{r}
#| label: equal-estimates
free <- fit_sem(full, d, meanstructure = TRUE, information = "expected")
shared <- intersect(names(free@theta), names(fx@theta))
c(estimates = max(abs(free@theta[shared] - fx@theta[shared])),
  standard_errors = max(abs(sqrt(diag(free@vcov))[shared] - sqrt(diag(fx@vcov))[shared])))
```

```{r}
#| label: equal-estimates-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(max(abs(free@theta[shared] - fx@theta[shared])) < 1e-8,
          max(abs(sqrt(diag(free@vcov))[shared] - sqrt(diag(fx@vcov))[shared])) < 1e-8)
```

The estimates and standard errors agree to rounding. Step 3 is the claim that the information has no cross block;
look at the free fit's information between the fixed moments and the structural parameters, in the engine's
raw coordinates, for both kinds of information:

```{r}
#| label: cross-block
ram <- free@internals$ram
smp <- medfit:::.sem_sample(free@data, ram)
info_e <- medfit:::.sem_info_expected(free@theta, ram, smp, NULL)
info_o <- medfit:::.sem_info_observed(free@theta, ram, smp, NULL)
moment_names <- c("treatment~~treatment", "treatment~~covariate1", "covariate1~~covariate1",
                  "treatment~1", "covariate1~1")
structural <- setdiff(rownames(info_e), moment_names)
cross <- function(m) max(abs(m[moment_names, structural]))
cross_table <- data.frame(
  information = c("expected", "observed"),
  cross_block_largest_entry = c(cross(info_e), cross(info_o)),
  largest_entry_of_the_matrix = c(max(abs(info_e)), max(abs(info_o)))
)
cross_table$orders_of_magnitude_below <- round(log10(cross_table$largest_entry_of_the_matrix /
                                                       cross_table$cross_block_largest_entry), 1)
cross_table
```

```{r}
#| label: cross-block-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(cross(info_e) < 1e-10 * max(abs(info_e)), cross(info_o) < 1e-6 * max(abs(info_o)))
```

The cross block has `r length(moment_names)` $\times$ `r length(structural)` entries. Its largest entry is
`r cross_table$orders_of_magnitude_below[1]` orders of magnitude below the largest entry of the matrix for the expected
information and `r cross_table$orders_of_magnitude_below[2]` for the observed one (which the engine computes by finite
differences of the gradient, so it carries a numerical error that the expected one does not). Both are zero to numerical
precision, as Step 3 says.

### Fixing a subset

With `fixed_x = "treatment"`, only the moments that involve `treatment` are fixed: its mean, its variance
and its covariance with `covariate1`. The variance and the mean of `covariate1` stay free. The structural
parameters keep their estimates and standard errors; the free moments of `covariate1` keep their estimates
but not their standard errors:

```{r}
#| label: subset
subset_fit <- fit_sem(full, d, meanstructure = TRUE, fixed_x = "treatment", information = "expected")
both <- intersect(names(free@theta), names(subset_fit@theta))
own_moments <- c("covariate1~~covariate1", "covariate1~1")
se_change <- sqrt(diag(subset_fit@vcov))[both] - sqrt(diag(free@vcov))[both]
c(structural_estimates = max(abs(subset_fit@theta[structural] - free@theta[structural])),
  structural_standard_errors = max(abs(se_change[structural])),
  covariate1_moment_estimates = max(abs(subset_fit@theta[own_moments] - free@theta[own_moments])))
signif(se_change[own_moments], 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: subset-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(max(abs(subset_fit@theta[structural] - free@theta[structural])) < 1e-8,
          max(abs(se_change[structural])) < 1e-8,
          max(abs(subset_fit@theta[own_moments] - free@theta[own_moments])) < 1e-8,
          all(abs(se_change[own_moments]) > 1e-5))
```

The reason is the information of the exogenous block itself. In the free fit the standard error of a
free moment $j$ is $\sqrt{(I^{-1})_{j j}}$ over the whole exogenous block, and that block is not diagonal.
Under normality the means and the (co)variances share no information (Chapter 1, Section 8), but within
the means $\Sigma^{-1}$ couples the mean of `covariate1` with the mean of `treatment`, and within the
(co)variances the variance of `covariate1` shares information with the variance of `treatment` and with
their covariance. Fixing the moments of `treatment` removes those partners, so the standard errors of
`covariate1`'s moments come from a smaller block. For the mean this has a closed form. With $s_{11}$,
$s_{12}$, $s_{22}$ the entries of $S_{ff}$ (1 for `treatment`, 2 for `covariate1`), the free fit's standard
error is $\sqrt{s_{22}/n}$ and the subset fit's is $\sqrt{(s_{22} - s_{12}^2/s_{11})/n}$, the conditional
variance of `covariate1` given `treatment`, over $n$:

```{r}
#| label: subset-mean
se_mean <- function(f) sqrt(diag(f@vcov))[["covariate1~1"]]
c(free_fit = se_mean(free), by_hand_free = sqrt(s_ff[2, 2] / n),
  subset_fit = se_mean(subset_fit), by_hand_subset = sqrt((s_ff[2, 2] - s_ff[1, 2]^2 / s_ff[1, 1]) / n))
```

```{r}
#| label: subset-mean-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(abs(se_mean(free) - sqrt(s_ff[2, 2] / n)) < 1e-6,
          abs(se_mean(subset_fit) - sqrt((s_ff[2, 2] - s_ff[1, 2]^2 / s_ff[1, 1]) / n)) < 1e-6)
```

The structural block still has no cross term with any exogenous moment, so Step 3 holds for it unchanged.

## 4. The conditional log likelihood

`logLik()` for the fixed fit is the *conditional* log likelihood $\ell_c(\hat\psi)$. From Step 1,
$\ell_c = \ell - \ell_m(\eta)$, so at the estimates

$$
\ell_c(\hat\psi) = \ell(\hat\psi, \hat\eta) - \ell_m(\hat\eta) .
$$

**The marginal term.** Evaluate $\ell_m$ at the sample moments. Each row contributes
$-\tfrac12\bigl[k\log 2\pi + \log|S_{ff}| + (x_i - \bar x)^\top S_{ff}^{-1}(x_i - \bar x)\bigr]$. By the trace argument of
Chapter 1 (Step 3), $\sum_i (x_i - \bar x)^\top S_{ff}^{-1}(x_i - \bar x) = n\operatorname{tr}(S_{ff}^{-1} S_{ff}) = n k$. So

$$
\ell_m(\hat\eta) = -\frac n2 \bigl(\log|S_{ff}| + k + k\log 2\pi\bigr),
\qquad
\ell_c(\hat\psi) = \ell(\hat\psi, \hat\eta) + \frac n2 \bigl(\log|S_{ff}| + k + k\log 2\pi\bigr).
$$

This is the correction `logLik()` applies to the joint value. Check it three ways: against the joint value from the free
fit, against a direct computation of the conditional density from the RAM matrices, and against lavaan.

```{r}
#| label: conditional
k <- length(exo)
marginal <- -0.5 * n * (as.numeric(determinant(s_ff, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus) + k + k * log(2 * pi))
c(joint_logLik_free_fit = as.numeric(logLik(free)),
  conditional_logLik_fixed_fit = as.numeric(logLik(fx)),
  difference_of_the_two = as.numeric(logLik(fx)) - as.numeric(logLik(free)),
  minus_marginal_term = -marginal)
```

```{r}
#| label: conditional-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(abs(as.numeric(logLik(fx)) - as.numeric(logLik(free)) + marginal) < 1e-6)
```

By hand from the conditional model of the setup: the endogenous block is `mediator1` and `outcome`, the mean of each
row given its fixed variables is $c + \Gamma x_i$ and the covariance is $\Psi$. Sum the bivariate normal log densities:

```{r}
#| label: conditional-by-hand
mats <- medfit:::.sem_ram_mats(fx@internals$ram, fx@theta)
A <- mats$a
s_ram <- mats$s
m <- medfit:::.sem_ram_m(fx@internals$ram, fx@theta)
vars <- fx@internals$ram$vars
endo <- c("mediator1", "outcome")
iy <- match(endo, vars)
ix <- match(exo, vars)
b_yy <- solve(diag(length(endo)) - A[iy, iy])
Psi <- b_yy %*% s_ram[iy, iy] %*% t(b_yy)
data_mat <- as.matrix(d[, c(endo, exo)])
ll_by_hand <- sum(vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
  mu_i <- drop(b_yy %*% (m[iy] + A[iy, ix] %*% data_mat[i, exo]))
  e <- data_mat[i, endo] - mu_i
  -0.5 * (length(endo) * log(2 * pi) + log(det(Psi)) + drop(t(e) %*% solve(Psi) %*% e))
}, numeric(1)))
c(by_hand = ll_by_hand, logLik = as.numeric(logLik(fx)))
```

```{r}
#| label: conditional-by-hand-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(abs(ll_by_hand - as.numeric(logLik(fx))) < 1e-6)
```

**The parameter count.** `logLik()` also carries a `df` attribute, the parameter count behind AIC and BIC. With
a mean structure the free intercepts are in the parameter vector already. Without one, the likelihood still has
means: the model's means are saturated, one free mean for each variable that is not fixed (a fixed variable's mean is a
constant, not a parameter). So the count is

$$
\text{df}_{\text{logLik}} = (q - \text{rank}) + (p - k)\,\mathbb 1[\text{no mean structure}] ,
$$

with $q - \text{rank}$ the free parameters after equality constraints. Check against the four fits of Section 2, and
compare with lavaan, which reports the same count for the mean-structure fit:

```{r}
#| label: ll-df
ll <- lapply(fits, logLik)
data.frame(
  fit = names(fits),
  logLik = vapply(ll, as.numeric, numeric(1)),
  df_attribute = vapply(ll, attr, numeric(1), "df"),
  formula = vapply(fits, function(f) {
    p <- length(f@internals$ram$obs)
    kk <- length(f@internals$fixed_x)
    (length(f@theta) - f@internals$eq_rank) + (p - kk) * !isTRUE(f@internals$ram$has_mean)
  }, numeric(1)),
  AIC = vapply(fits, AIC, numeric(1)),
  BIC = vapply(fits, BIC, numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

```{r}
#| label: ll-df-check
#| include: false
ll_df <- vapply(ll, attr, numeric(1), "df")
stopifnot(identical(unname(ll_df), c(13, 8, 13, 8)),
          abs(as.numeric(ll$fixed_cov) - as.numeric(ll$fixed_mean)) < 1e-6,
          abs(as.numeric(ll$free_cov) - as.numeric(ll$free_mean)) < 1e-6)
```

The two fixed fits have the same likelihood, parameter count, AIC and BIC whether or not a mean structure is
declared, and so do the two free fits: declaring means only moves the intercepts into the parameter vector.

```{r}
#| label: lavaan
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)
lv_fixed <- lavaan::sem(restricted, d, meanstructure = TRUE, fixed.x = TRUE, information = "expected")
lv_free <- lavaan::sem(restricted, d, meanstructure = TRUE, fixed.x = FALSE, information = "expected")
lv_row <- function(f) {
  unname(c(lavaan::fitMeasures(f, "logl"), lavaan::fitMeasures(f, "npar"), lavaan::fitMeasures(f, "chisq"),
           lavaan::fitMeasures(f, "df"), lavaan::fitMeasures(f, "aic"), lavaan::fitMeasures(f, "bic")))
}
mf_row <- function(f) {
  unname(c(as.numeric(logLik(f)), attr(logLik(f), "df"), f@n_obs * f@f, f@df, AIC(f), BIC(f)))
}
data.frame(
  quantity = c("logLik", "df of logLik (lavaan: npar)", "chisq", "df", "AIC", "BIC"),
  medfit_fixed = mf_row(fits$fixed_mean),
  lavaan_fixed.x_TRUE = lv_row(lv_fixed),
  medfit_free = mf_row(fits$free_mean),
  lavaan_fixed.x_FALSE = lv_row(lv_free)
)
mean_fixed_expected <- fit_sem(restricted, d, meanstructure = TRUE, fixed_x = TRUE, information = "expected")
nm <- intersect(names(lavaan::coef(lv_fixed)), names(mean_fixed_expected@theta))
c(largest_estimate_difference = max(abs(lavaan::coef(lv_fixed)[nm] - mean_fixed_expected@theta[nm])),
  largest_se_difference = max(abs(sqrt(diag(lavaan::vcov(lv_fixed)))[nm] - sqrt(diag(mean_fixed_expected@vcov))[nm])))
```

```{r}
#| label: lavaan-check
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)
stopifnot(max(abs(mf_row(fits$fixed_mean) - lv_row(lv_fixed))) < 1e-5,
          max(abs(mf_row(fits$free_mean) - lv_row(lv_free))) < 1e-5,
          max(abs(lavaan::coef(lv_fixed)[nm] - mean_fixed_expected@theta[nm])) < 1e-6)
```

(Both standard-error computations use the expected information.)

OpenMx can hold the exogenous moments at their sample values with fixed paths. Its `-2 log L` is the *joint* value
at those moments, so it equals the free fit's, and the conditional value differs from it by the marginal term:

```{r}
#| label: openmx
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("OpenMx", quietly = TRUE)
suppressMessages(library(OpenMx))
mxOption(NULL, "Number of Threads", 1)
dat <- d[, c("mediator1", "treatment", "covariate1", "outcome")]
mu_s <- colMeans(dat)
s_s <- cov(dat) * (n - 1) / n
mod <- mxModel(
  "fixedx", type = "RAM", manifestVars = names(dat),
  mxPath("treatment", "mediator1", values = 0.4, labels = "a"),
  mxPath("covariate1", "mediator1", values = 0.1, labels = "m_c"),
  mxPath("mediator1", "outcome", values = 0.4, labels = "b"),
  mxPath("covariate1", "outcome", values = 0.1, labels = "y_c"),
  mxPath(c("mediator1", "outcome"), arrows = 2, values = 1, labels = c("vm", "vy")),
  mxPath("treatment", arrows = 2, free = FALSE, values = s_s["treatment", "treatment"]),
  mxPath("covariate1", arrows = 2, free = FALSE, values = s_s["covariate1", "covariate1"]),
  mxPath("treatment", "covariate1", arrows = 2, free = FALSE, values = s_s["treatment", "covariate1"]),
  mxPath("one", c("treatment", "covariate1"), free = FALSE, values = mu_s[c("treatment", "covariate1")]),
  mxPath("one", c("mediator1", "outcome"), values = 0, labels = c("i_m", "i_y")),
  mxData(dat, type = "raw")
)
mx_run <- mxRun(mod, silent = TRUE)
data.frame(
  quantity = c("OpenMx -2 log L (joint, moments held)", "medfit free fit, -2 log L (joint)",
               "medfit fixed fit, -2 log L (conditional)", "conditional + 2 x marginal term"),
  value = c(summary(mx_run)$Minus2LogLikelihood, -2 * as.numeric(logLik(fits$free_mean)),
            -2 * as.numeric(logLik(fits$fixed_mean)), -2 * as.numeric(logLik(fits$fixed_mean)) - 2 * marginal)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: openmx-check
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("OpenMx", quietly = TRUE)
stopifnot(abs(summary(mx_run)$Minus2LogLikelihood + 2 * as.numeric(logLik(fits$free_mean))) < 1e-3,
          abs(-2 * as.numeric(logLik(fits$fixed_mean)) - 2 * marginal - summary(mx_run)$Minus2LogLikelihood) < 1e-3)
```

(Here `cp == 0` is the restriction, written in OpenMx by leaving out the path from `treatment` to `outcome`.)

## 5. What the engine refuses

Because $\ell_c$ conditions on different variables for different fixed sets, two such values do not measure the same
thing. The difference of two of them, or two AIC values, is meaningless, so the engine refuses to produce it. The
messages (captured with `tryCatch` so the page keeps rendering):

```{r}
#| label: refusals
say <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch({
    expr
    "no error"
  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
}
fixed_full <- fit_sem(full, d, fixed_x = TRUE)
fixed_restricted <- fit_sem(restricted, d, fixed_x = TRUE)
free_restricted <- fit_sem(restricted, d)
fixed_treatment <- fit_sem(restricted, d, fixed_x = "treatment")
d_other <- d
d_other$outcome <- d_other$outcome + 1
fixed_other_data <- fit_sem(restricted, d_other, fixed_x = TRUE)
msgs <- c(
  `anova, fixed vs free` = say(anova(fixed_restricted, free_restricted)),
  `AIC, fixed vs free` = say(AIC(fixed_restricted, free_restricted)),
  `BIC, free vs fixed` = say(BIC(free_restricted, fixed_restricted)),
  `AIC, different fixed sets` = say(AIC(fixed_restricted, fixed_treatment)),
  `AIC, fixed fit vs an lm` = say(AIC(fixed_restricted, lm(outcome ~ treatment, d))),
  `anova, same set, different data` = say(anova(fixed_full, fixed_other_data)),
  `AIC, same set, different data` = say(AIC(fixed_full, fixed_other_data))
)
cat(sprintf("%s:\n  %s\n", names(msgs), msgs), sep = "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: refusals-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(!any(msgs == "no error"))
```

Comparisons within one fixed set and one data set are allowed, and they are exactly what the free fits would give:

```{r}
#| label: allowed
anova(fixed_full, fixed_restricted)
free_full <- fit_sem(full, d)
anova(free_full, free_restricted)
```

```{r}
#| label: allowed-check
#| include: false
diff_fixed <- anova(fixed_full, fixed_restricted)$`Chisq diff`[2]
diff_free <- anova(free_full, free_restricted)$`Chisq diff`[2]
stopifnot(abs(diff_fixed - diff_free) < 1e-6)
```

The two tables are the same test: the chi-square difference of a nested pair does not depend on whether the exogenous
moments are fixed.

Two more refusals concern the model itself. A statement about a selected variable's moments contradicts the request to
fix them, and a name that is not exogenous cannot be fixed:

```{r}
#| label: model-errors
msgs <- c(
  `statement on a fixed variable` = say(fit_sem(paste0(full, "treatment ~~ treatment\n"), d, fixed_x = TRUE)),
  `fixed_x names the outcome` = say(fit_sem(full, d, fixed_x = "outcome"))
)
cat(sprintf("%s:\n  %s\n", names(msgs), msgs), sep = "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: model-errors-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(!any(msgs == "no error"))
```

Finally, `mbco_sem()` (the test of an indirect effect of Chapter 5) refits the model text on the data the fit used, with the fit's `fixed_x`. The statistic is
the same as from the free fit, since the structural estimates and the discrepancy are:

```{r}
#| label: mbco
c(from_fixed_fit = unname(mbco_sem(fixed_full, "a", "b")$statistic),
  from_free_fit = unname(mbco_sem(fit_sem(full, d), "a", "b")$statistic))
```

```{r}
#| label: mbco-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(abs(mbco_sem(fixed_full, "a", "b")$statistic - mbco_sem(fit_sem(full, d), "a", "b")$statistic) < 1e-6)
```

## 6. When to use it

Fixing the exogenous moments shrinks the problem: with many covariates the free fit has a parameter for every
variance and covariance among them, and the fixed fit has none, so it is smaller. The price is the
likelihood: it is conditional, comparable only within one fixed set and one data set, and it is not the joint
likelihood a different package may report. When the question is about the paths (their estimates, standard errors,
tests) the answer is the same either way, as Section 3 proved; the standard errors of exogenous moments
left free next to fixed ones are the exception that section showed. When the question is about information criteria across
models, fit them all with the same `fixed_x`.

**The default since 0.15.0.** An unset `fixed_x` is not `FALSE` any more: it resolves to the exogenous observed
variables, except those a `~~` or `~1` statement names (a lenient subset with a message; an explicit `TRUE` still refuses
such a statement, Section 5), and an unset `meanstructure` is `TRUE`. The chapters of this book call the engine through
the `fit_sem()` wrapper defined in their setup chunk, which pins the 0.14.x settings (`fixed_x = FALSE,
meanstructure = NULL`) so the matrices they take apart stay the joint, covariance-first ones. Here is the one place
where the unpinned call is used, to show what the default changes and what it leaves alone:

```{r}
#| label: default-vs-pinned
default_fit <- medfit::fit_sem(full, d)                                         # the 0.15.0 defaults
pinned_fit <- medfit::fit_sem(full, d, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL)   # the 0.14.x behavior
paths <- c("a", "b", "cp")
list(
  fixed_by_default = glance(default_fit)$fixed_x,
  structural_estimates_differ_by = max(abs(coef(default_fit)[paths] - coef(pinned_fit)[paths])),
  standard_errors_differ_by = max(abs(sqrt(diag(vcov(default_fit)))[paths] - sqrt(diag(vcov(pinned_fit)))[paths])),
  logLik = c(default = as.numeric(logLik(default_fit)), pinned = as.numeric(logLik(pinned_fit))),
  npar = c(default = attr(logLik(default_fit), "df"), pinned = attr(logLik(pinned_fit), "df")),
  AIC = c(default = AIC(default_fit), pinned = AIC(pinned_fit)),
  coef_names_default = names(coef(default_fit)),
  coef_names_pinned = names(coef(pinned_fit))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: default-vs-pinned-check
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  identical(glance(default_fit)$fixed_x, "treatment, covariate1"),
  max(abs(coef(default_fit)[paths] - coef(pinned_fit)[paths])) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(sqrt(diag(vcov(default_fit)))[paths] - sqrt(diag(vcov(pinned_fit)))[paths])) < 1e-6,
  attr(logLik(default_fit), "df") < attr(logLik(pinned_fit), "df"),
  !any(grepl("treatment~~", names(coef(default_fit)), fixed = TRUE))
)
```

What moves: the conditional log likelihood, the parameter count behind AIC and BIC, the names in `coef()` (the fixed
moments leave them, the intercepts enter), and which random start a multi-start fit tries. What does not move: the
structural estimates and their standard errors, as Section 3 proved. AIC and BIC from the default fit equal those of
`lavaan::sem(..., meanstructure = TRUE)` with `fixed.x = TRUE`; against a default `lavaan::sem()`, which has no mean
structure, medfit's AIC is larger by $2k$ and its BIC by $k \log n$, with $k$ the number of unfixed observed means
(here two intercepts). The schedule and the evidence are in
[Native defaults in 0.15.0](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/articles/native-defaults-0-15.html);
`options(medfit.native_defaults)` is obsolete and is removed in 0.16.0.

## Check yourself

1. In Section 3 where does the proof use that no statement is made about the fixed variables' moments? (Answer: Step 2
   needs no parameter or constraint shared between $\psi$ and $\eta$. A constraint linking a moment to a path ties them,
   and then the structural estimates change. A fixed value such as `treatment ~~ 0.25*treatment` leaves the structural
   estimates alone but restricts $\eta$, so the discrepancy and the chi-square change. The engine refuses both kinds of
   statement.)
2. With $p = 6$ observed variables, $k = 3$ fixed, no mean structure, and 11 free parameters after constraints, what is the
   `df` of `logLik()`? (Answer: $11 + (6 - 3) = 14$.)
3. The fixed and the free fit report different `logLik()` values for the same model and data. Which is wrong? (Answer: neither:
   they are different quantities, the conditional and the joint log likelihood, and differ by the marginal term of Section 4.)
